 Casper Ruud Opens Up: “Last Year, I No Longer Felt Like Getting Up and Training”
 November 6, 2026 05:10 PM by Luca Ferrante Add as preferred source on Google SHARE © Instagram Tennis Tv/fair use The life of a professional tennis player involves a range of difficulties and challenges that fans cannot naturally perceive through a screen or while watching matches. Maintaining a consistent level throughout an entire season is far from straightforward—something made to look easier by the standards set by the Big Three, and more recently by players such as Jannik Sinner, Carlos Alcaraz and Alexander Zverev.
 ADVERTISEMENT
 The point was highlighted by Casper Ruud in a lengthy interview with L’Équipe . The Norwegian is attempting to finish the season strongly at the Paris Masters, where he has reached the quarter-finals.
 Speaking about life as a tennis player, Ruud said: “The most difficult thing is that it’s a very monotonous and repetitive life. Training can be enjoyable, but it can also become exhausting. Matches are obviously exciting, but they are also mentally demanding. We have so many mandatory tournaments that we don’t get long periods of training—the kind of periods that really allow you to improve.”
 Ruud’s struggles in 2025
 On the extremely demanding schedule, the Norwegian revealed that he experienced significant difficulties in 2025.
 “You don’t have time to breathe, go home for a month or two and really train. The only time you can do that is during the break between seasons. Even then, if you play in the ATP Finals, you finish at the end of November and have to be ready for the start of January in Australia.
 ADVERTISEMENT
 “All of that led me last year to reach a point where I no longer wanted to get up and go training when the alarm went off in the morning.”
 Ruud’s thoughts on modern tennis
 After his impressive victory over Jan-Lennard Struff, Ruud shared his thoughts on the current state of tennis in an interview with Tennis Channel .
 “There won’t be as many great matches in modern tennis because everyone serves well, returns well and attacks whenever they see an opening. I haven’t always had the courage to attempt big shots when I saw a real opportunity.
 “I was a little passive because my game was more focused on gradually wearing down my opponent, perhaps waiting for them to make a mistake. You see the other players and, nowadays, they hit the ball however they want. I’m trying to do a little more with my tennis.
 ADVERTISEMENT
 “It’s a continuous challenge, and it probably will be for the rest of my career.”
